output.title: Aerobic Base Run + Flat Strides
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy jog in Zone 1 → 35 min steady aerobic running in Zone 2 → 5 x 20s fast relaxed flat strides with 40s easy walk recoveries → Cool down 5 min easy walk and mobility. Overall: Aerobic foundation run with relaxed neuromuscular flat strides to open Week 1 smoothly. This establishes running rhythm without accumulating systemic fatigue on flat pavement. Reason: Initiates the 16-week marathon cycle on Wednesday with controlled aerobic volume, introducing neuromuscular turnover via flat strides without hills. Benefit: Enhances lipid oxidation enzymes, capillary density, and reinforces efficient motor unit recruitment without cardiovascular strain. Warning: Strides are fast and relaxed, not all-out sprints; terminate immediately if you feel any hamstring or calf tightness.
output.fueling_tip: Sessions < 75 mins: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); no exogenous carbs needed.

output.title: Bodyweight Strength & Single-Leg Stability
output.description: Process: Warm up 5 min dynamic mobility and activation drills → Bodyweight Squats: 3x10, 90s rest → Alternating Reverse Lunges: 3x10 each leg, 90s rest → Single-Leg Glute Bridges: 3x12 each leg, 60s rest → Step-Ups onto sturdy knee-height bench: 3x10 each leg, 90s rest → Plank hold: 3x45s, 60s rest → Cool down 5 min full-body mobility and calf stretching. Overall: Targeted bodyweight strength session to build musculoskeletal resilience and pelvic stability for marathon training. Every exercise uses dedicated straight sets with prescribed rests. Reason: Introduces fundamental chassis strength early in the Base phase without gym equipment, protecting tendons and joints against repetitive flat road impact. Benefit: Strengthens kinetic chain recruitment, increases single-leg stability, and promotes bone mineral density and connective tissue stiffness. Warning: Prioritize strict alignment and slow eccentric control on lunges and step-ups; avoid knee cave-in or arch collapse.
output.fueling_tip: Sessions < 75 mins: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); no exogenous carbs needed.

output.title: Aerobic Recovery Run
output.description: Process: Warm up 5 min brisk walk and light dynamic drills → 35 min continuous easy recovery running in Zone 1 → Cool down 5 min walking and lower-leg stretching. Overall: Low-intensity recovery run dedicated to active flushing and peripheral capillary blood flow between strength work and the weekend long run. Keep effort conversational and light. Reason: Scheduled between Thursday's structural strength session and Saturday's longer effort to ensure zero accumulated fatigue. Benefit: Stimulates active recovery, clears metabolic waste, and maintains movement continuity without raising cortisol. Warning: Strictly avoid drifting into Zone 2; if heart rate approaches 130 bpm, drop pace immediately to maintain pure recovery effort.
output.fueling_tip: Sessions < 75 mins: Plain water and optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); no exogenous carbs needed.

output.title: Aerobic Base Long Run
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy walking and gradual jogging below 130 bpm → 70 min steady aerobic running strictly capped below AeT in Zone 2 → Cool down 5 min easy walking and static stretching. Overall: Foundational weekend long run executed on flat road terrain at steady aerobic effort. Keeps well below the 33% weekly volume cap while building endurance. Reason: Establishes aerobic duration and lipid oxidation capacity tailored to the flat City Marathon profile. Benefit: Expands mitochondrial mass, increases stroke volume, and builds structural bone and tendon resilience for prolonged road running. Warning: Do not race or surge late in the run; hold a steady, disciplined pace and respect the upper AeT ceiling of 145 bpm.
output.fueling_tip: Sessions 75-150 mins: 30-60g carbohydrates per hour + 300-500mg sodium/hr with 400-600ml water/hr.

output.title: Scheduled Rest & Full Restoration
output.description: Process: Full complete rest day with zero running or strength training → Gentle 10 min evening mobility and tissue release. Overall: Total physiological rest day to allow muscle protein synthesis, glycogen supercompensation, and autonomic nervous system replenishment. Reason: Concludes the partial opening week, ensuring 5 total training days per week preference is strictly met while preparing the body for Week 2 progression. Benefit: Lowers systemic cortisol, restores muscle glycogen stores, and promotes soft tissue remodeling. Warning: Resist the temptation to cross-train; complete non-impact rest is critical for full systemic recovery.
output.fueling_tip: Focus on nutrient-dense meals with adequate carbohydrate availability (4-6g CHO/kg bodyweight) and lean protein to support recovery and hormonal health.
